name: Tutor
seoDescription: Calculate estimated business insurance costs for tutor businesses including general liability and professional E&O coverage.

industryContext.contextNote: Tutors work one-on-one or in small groups with students, often minors, giving them a distinct liability profile centered on supervision and educational outcomes rather than physical trade risk.

riskFactors.title: Student Supervision Claims
riskFactors.description: Tutors working with minors carry supervision-related liability if a student is injured or a safety incident occurs during a session.

riskFactors.title: Educational Outcome Disputes
riskFactors.description: Parents or students who feel tutoring failed to deliver promised academic results can raise disputes over fees or service quality.

riskFactors.title: In-Home Session Liability
riskFactors.description: Tutors who travel to a student's home or host sessions in their own space face premises-related liability distinct from a school setting.

faqs.question: Why do tutors need General Liability insurance?
faqs.answer: General Liability covers bodily injury or property damage that could occur during an in-person tutoring session, whether at the tutor's location or the student's home.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a tutor?
faqs.answer: A tutor in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $250 per year for baseline General Liability coverage, one of the lowest tiers modeled here.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with children need special coverage?
faqs.answer: Tutors working with minors should confirm their Professional Liability policy addresses supervision-related claims, since working with children carries added scrutiny.

faqs.question: Is online-only tutoring lower risk than in-person tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, online tutoring generally carries lower premises and supervision risk, though Professional Liability for educational outcome disputes still applies to both formats.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Tutors carry a 0.85 actuarial risk factor, reflecting low physical hazard balanced against supervision-related liability, particularly when working with minors.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with revenue tier and Professional Liability endorsements covering educational service disputes.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Tutor premiums are among the lowest of any profession modeled here, comparable to mobile notaries and translators.
